config.label: RIK e-arveldaja API key ID
config.description: RIK e-arveldaja API key ID. Can alternatively be supplied via a .env file or an apikey*.txt file in the working directory.

config.label: RIK e-arveldaja API public value
config.description: RIK e-arveldaja API public value. Can alternatively be supplied via a .env file or an apikey*.txt file in the working directory.

config.label: RIK e-arveldaja API password (HMAC signing secret)
config.description: RIK e-arveldaja API password (HMAC signing secret). Can alternatively be supplied via a .env file or an apikey*.txt file in the working directory.

config.label: Which RIK server to target
config.description: Which RIK server to target. "live" (default) or "demo".

config.label: Platform-separated (colon on Linux/macOS, semicolon on Windows) list of directories that file-reading tools are allowed to read from
config.description: Platform-separated (colon on Linux/macOS, semicolon on Windows) list of directories that file-reading tools are allowed to read from. Replaces the default (the working directory and the OS temp dir); EARVELDAJA_ALLOW_HOME is ignored when set.

config.label: Set to "1" or "true" to disable MCP progress notifications
config.description: Set to "1" or "true" to disable MCP progress notifications. Workaround for clients that close the stdio transport when a progress notification arrives after the matching response has been processed.

config.label: Connection a freshly started server activates when several are configured: an index or the exact connection name shown by list_connections
config.description: Connection a freshly started server activates when several are configured: an index or the exact connection name shown by list_connections. Default: index 0. An unknown value fails startup instead of silently using index 0.

config.label: Absolute path to a regular file
config.description: Absolute path to a regular file. When set, everything the server writes to stderr is also appended to this file (mode 0o600). Off by default. Cross-platform. Useful when the MCP host swallows stderr. Pipes, devices, sockets, /dev/stdout, and /proc/self/fd/* are refused so the tee cannot corrupt the MCP stdio transport.
